chapter: Nola band, day job and nightclub work
title: Personnel and character of the Iberville nightclub band
summary: The five-piece band had two saxophones, piano and drummer; LaCaze needed arrangements; the job was pitiful.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah, yeah. See everybody at night. We were taking a nap. Well, they had a couple of entertainers around there, singers, dancers, and had a piano player. He was a man of piano. Yeah, I'll tell you. Hoyford Smith was a saxophone player, an alto saxophone, and Thomas Parker was playing the tenor saxophone.

Well, they had this on account of hard to find people, you know, musicians. I see. They had to keep what kind of kids. And there's one more I could remember. See, Parker, Hoyford Smith, I called them to you. They had a piano too, huh? And they had a piano. I can't remember his name. It was a man. I don't remember anything. And Ellie Begold, he was on the drum. Anyhow, there was about five. That's about all I remember. That makes fun, yeah. Yeah.
You said that was, did you, was that a reading band, or yes, a jazz band?

Well, it was kind of mixed up. Oh, they did have a few arrangements. Yeah. Yeah, yeah. I'll tell you what, I had to, wherever I went, I had to bring some arrangements with me, because I couldn't just do without it.
You know, I needed them, I had to have some music. I see. In other words, you played mostly for music.
Oh, yeah, see. I'd done some of this work without the music, but the biggest part of my work I'd done was with the music, you see.
In that place did you play for a show, or was it just dancing?

Well, it was, no, it was just a nightclub, like. And they had a couple of entertainers there to sing, some women, and do a little dancing. I don't know, I forgot the name of the club, but the man's name, his name was Cialina, Johnny Cialina. I mentioned that because I thought probably might.
We can figure out what that is. We can figure it out. From the location and everything.
Well, they've got books you can look, you'd be surprised at what you can look up in a book.
Yeah, you know, working in the library, we have them. I knew you were a blacksmith.

Yeah, I guess too. They had that in a book? Yeah, I guess. You just... The city directory? Yeah, get it like, you get this information from me now. Yeah. And you talk to other people, and the people who know you, and they'll say, well I know that guy, he's a blacksmith. Yeah. Or he was a fisherman or something like that.
That was one of your longest jobs in music then. Yeah. Six months. Yeah, yeah, yeah, about the month of the long.
For a steady job like that, it must have been awful.
